newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan army on standby for transport strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan army on standby for transport strike.

text.p: Venezuela's army is ready to step in should a threatened nationwide transport strike go ahead on Monday, Defence Minister Pedro Nicolas Valencia said on Friday.
The plan to have soldiers drive buses and subway trains would be used "only if all the other means to solve this problem have been tried," Valencia told reporters at Miraflores presidential palace.
Transport unions said on Friday they would escalate a strike to the national level if the government did not meet calls for a 50 percent increase in bus fares.
"We are very sorry for the users but we are in a conflict situation and we won't stop until we have something to offer the workers," bus union president Raul Maldonado told reporters.

The government has agreed to a 30 percent hike in fares. But bus drivers in Caracas suburbs have been on strike since Wednesday after the Transport Ministry turned down requests for a further 20 percent increase.
